preparation_rules: Strip leaves from tough stems: The thick central stems are woody and fibrous. Strip off air bladders and leaf-like fronds.
Wash and soak thoroughly: Soak in fresh water for 10-15 minutes to clear sand, debris, and excess salt.
Parboil or boil to soften: Boiling or pickling in acid neutralizes bitterness and tenderizes the dense plant walls.

recipes.title: Pickled Sargassum muticum & Potato Soup
recipes.description: A creamy potato soup featuring Sargassum muticum fronds pickled in apple cider vinegar and honey.
ingredients: 1 large handful fresh Sargassum muticum fronds (cleaned)
1 L vegetable stock or chicken stock
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Submerge fresh S. muticum fronds in cold fresh water for 10 minutes to remove sand and salt residue. Drain well.
Bring 900 mL water, apple cider vinegar, and honey to a boil in a pot. Place the washed seaweed fronds in a heatproof bowl and pour the boiling vinegar mixture over top to steep.
Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add chopped onions and cubed potatoes; cook gently for 2 minutes. Pour in stock and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until potatoes are fork-tender.

Strain a handful of pickled S. muticum and drop into the simmering soup. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes. Remove from heat and blend smooth using an immersion stick blender. Season with salt and black pepper.

recipes.title: Crispy Pan-Fried Sargassum muticum Fronds
recipes.description: Quickly fried stripped Sargassum muticum leaves served as crispy, umami-rich sea chips.
ingredients: 100 g fresh Sargassum muticum fronds (leaves and bladders only, stems discarded)
2 tbsp coconut oil or neutral cooking oil
instructions: Strip leaf-like structures and float bladders away from the central woody stem. Rinse thoroughly under cold water and pat completely dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add stripped fronds in a single layer. Fry for 1 to 2 minutes until crisp and slightly darkened.
Transfer with a slotted spoon to paper towels to drain excess oil. Sprinkle immediately with sea salt and toasted sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Korean-Style Braised Sargassum (Sargassum-Jorim)
recipes.description: Sargassum fronds simmered in a soy, garlic, and sesame glaze to soften their texture and build savory depth.
instructions: Boil cleaned Sargassum muticum fronds in water for 3 to 5 minutes to soften. Drain and slice into bite-sized pieces.
In a saucepan, mix soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar, minced garlic, and water/dashi. Bring to a gentle boil.
Add the parboiled seaweed fronds to the pan. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15–20 minutes until the liquid reduces into a glossy glaze.
Stir in toasted sesame oil before removing from heat. Serve cold or warm as a side dish.
